newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul shares extend losses in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul shares extend losses in late trade.

text.p: Turkish stocks extended losses in late selling on Tuesday to test major support at the index's 1,550 level as the market was scared by rising uncertainities over the fate of the Islamist-led government, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 stood at 1,549 at 1251 GMT, down 2.09 percent from Monday's close.

"The market is gripped by uncertainty due to the expected resignation of (Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's) government. The index has support at the 1,550 level and the next support is seen is 1,530," said Ali Guler from Acar securities.
"Rising overnight (repo and money) rates negatively affected the market, too. I do not expect political uncertainty to fade much tomorrow," he added.

Members of the junior coalition partner True Path Party (DYP) and the Turkish press say Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist prime minister, will resign on Wednesday morning in a plan to swap jobs with Deputy Prime Minister and DYP leader Ciller and go to early elections before the end of the year.
But Erbakan made no specific mention of the plan in an hour-long speech to MPs of his Islam-based Welfare Party today.
A far-right leader with a key position in parliament said on Monday he would back government efforts to push the power transfer and election laws through parliament.
Anti-Islamist opposition, led by the army has brought the one-year-old Islamist-conservative coalition to the brink of collapse.
